literature_proposed.summary: A consequence of a published theorem, not formalised. The node's hypotheses (k^2 <= n < k^3, n = gcd(n,k)*q with q prime > k, minFac C(n,k) > k) imply those of erdos-1094--h2--h1--h1 (2k <= n < k^3, minFac C(n,k) > k; for k >= 2, k^2 >= 2k), so k is bounded by Konyagin's g(k) >= exp(c log^2 k) > k^3 for large k. The restriction does not make it elementary: no proof avoiding the analytic (fractional parts / short-interval primes) input is known to me. Exhaustive search (annex on this node) finds no example beyond the small k listed there, for k < 400.
